lines.text: Four years ago, this was AI video.
This is what four years did.
In 2022, research labs showed that plain words could become moving pictures.
But clips lasted a few seconds, and early animation drew every frame on its own.
So faces drifted. Objects melted. Nothing held still.
In 2023, Runway's Gen-2 put text-to-video into public hands.
Then, in February 2024, OpenAI previewed Sora, promising up to a minute of video.
Suddenly, a subject could hold together across a shot.
The race began. In June 2024 alone, Kling, Luma and Runway all showed new models.
By December, Sora was public, and Google's Veo 2 arrived a week later.
In May 2025, Veo 3 added generated sound.
Then came control: first and last frames, camera moves, and reference images that keep a character consistent.
Models even learned to edit real footage, adding, removing or restyling objects, not just inventing it.
Video stopped being a slot machine, and started becoming a tool.
By September 2026, developers announce thirty-second clips, native 4K, and sound generated with the picture.
Light behaves. Shots hold together for seconds, not frames.
Now the frame itself is changing. Genie 3 builds worlds you can steer, in real time.
Motion was the miracle. Now it's the baseline.
From melting pixels... to moving worlds.
